summary: Polished black marble crossed by fine pale veins, as on Art Deco lobbies, columns, floors and desk tops.
_comment: Polished black marble: a true black calcite marble with a fine network of pale veins, polished to a mirror. It is its own article and not a tint of a white marble: a dark tint on a white marble darkens its veins too, and this stone's veins are pale on black. The maps are the ambientCG scan Marble016 (tagged 'black, marble, reflective, shiny'), used as downloaded; the scan names no quarry, so the name says only Black ('nero marquina' is a search word, not a claim). SUBSURFACE, as the library's other marbles (Physically Based 'Marble' IOR, radius and radius scale), but a black stone absorbs nearly all the light that enters it: subsurface_weight is 0.1 and subsurface_color the scan's dark mean, so the scatter is all but invisible and the article reads by its polish and veins. The scan states no size: meters_per_tile 1.0 by judgement from its vein network (main veins 10 to 30 cm apart, hairlines between), the s1 option's length exactly, nothing stretched. Carries every relevant wear layer at 0 (C1): scratches (overlay 1, damage), dust as a deposit (Phase10), water spots, gated by the Crevice mask. Built by the Phase11 batch.
name: Marble_Black_Clean_Base_s1_v01

sources.note: The colour, roughness (mean 0.114, a polished face) and normal maps. Its mean linear albedo is (0.053, 0.058, 0.055).

specular_ior, subsurface_radius and subsurface_radius_scale are taken. base_color_const is not (the entry is a white marble; the scan's colour map carries the colour) and roughness 0 is not (the scan's own roughness map carries the polish).

sources.why: meters_per_tile 1.0 (the scan states no size; main veins 10 to 30 cm apart, as in slab marble); subsurface_weight 0.1 because a black stone absorbs nearly all the light that enters it; subsurface_color the scan's mean linear albedo.
